newsitem.title: USA: US savings and loans Q1 net $1.7 bln vs $1.8 bln.
newsitem.headline: US savings and loans Q1 net $1.7 bln vs $1.8 bln.

text.p: The U.S. savings and loan industry earned $1.7 billion in the first quarter of 1997, down from $1.8 billion in the same period last year and up from $1.5 billion in the fourth quarter of 1996, the U.S. Office of Thrift Supervision reported on Wednesday.

The thrift industry continued to shrink in the quarter, however. At the end of the first quarter 1,302 thrifts held total assets of $764.6 billion compared to 1,334 thrifts with total assets of $769.4 billion at the end of 1996.

Troubled assets increased slightly to $8.8 billion or 1.15 percent of total assets from $8.7 billion or 1.13 percent in the previous quarter, the OTS said. Comparative figures for the prior-year period were not immediately available.
OTS said troubled assets in the first quarter of 1996 totaled $9.4 billion, or 1.24 percent of total assets.
